summary: A conversation between two characters walking through a grove where walkways are suspended in oversized red maples, sitting on a birch-branch bench. The speaker confronts Ria about how she let Brautigan take his job and exile him to Siberia, while she describes the low-churn organization and its people being sent out into the world every decade. The excerpt is the middle of a longer story, Book 10 part 165, and its main points are the tension over a lost post and the hint of an upcoming meeting with one of the Great Old Ones.
one_line: Ria and a frustrated minister argue over his demotion by Brautigan while walking through a canopy-walkway grove toward a meeting with a Great Old One.
key_facts: The speaker says the organization's churn is incredibly low and that people are put back out into the world for a year every decade.
Ria says she has always lived off campus and commutes, and that she is not a team person.
The suspended walkways are strung from oversized red maples, with rope railings and basket platforms on pulleys.
The speaker notes that the trees are strangely oversized red maples without the whippy slenderness of the species.
Ria remarks that for a certain kind of person, the delightfulness of the walkways never wears off.
The birch-branch bench is described as a long twig-chair made from birch branches, rope and wire.
Ria says Viktor's schedule is his own and that if they are five minutes late, someone will put five minutes' worth of injecta into his in-box.
The speaker says Brautigan scooped his job and exiled him to Siberia, and that Ria went along with it.
The speaker says Ria could have stopped Brautigan with a word because the envoys from the vat-gods are the absolute monarchs at Ate.
The speaker describes himself as a minister without portfolio about to meet one of the Great Old Ones in his very vat, in person.
The speaker's hand and chest shake with bottled-up anger he had not dared admit.
Ria mentions an engineer living in Vierzon named Caleb.
